About the Role
This is a high-impact role that helps define how CoLab delivers technical value to its most strategic customers. You'll act as a dedicated technical problem-solver and trusted advisor, embedding with enterprise customers to optimize how they use CoLab—especially our AI tools.
You'll help large mechanical engineering orgs rethink how they manage feedback, data, and decision-making across design and PLM. That means getting deep into customer workflows, testing new ways of working, and building repeatable methods the rest of the team can scale.
You'll work within our forward deployed team, alongside a technical program manager, software FDE, and customer-facing teams to close technical gaps, shape product direction, and directly influence customer success. This role isn't about selling or pitching—it's about deeply understanding engineering problems and solving them alongside the customer.
Our Ideal Candidate
You're a mechanical engineer by trade but your superpower is applying that knowledge in creative, systems-level ways. You're curious, technical, and comfortable working through ambiguity. You've likely been a design engineer or worked in a PLM-heavy environment. Maybe you've dabbled in automation, scripting, or app development for internal tools.
You don't need to be the loudest voice in the room—but you can run a sprint, lead a cross-functional project, and talk shop with both customer engineers and internal developers.
If the average person might find this job too undefined or complex, that probably excites you.
Job Responsibilities
Embed with enterprise customers to optimize CoLab usage, with a focus on AI tools like AutoReview and Operator.
Investigate and solve complex engineering data and integration challenges across PLM, ERP, QMS, and traditional design feedback tools.
Partner with a cross functional team to test and implement new CoLab workflows inside customer environments
Collaborate with product teams to identify feature gaps, improve capabilities, and refine AutoReview
Build technical documentation, playbooks, and repeatable frameworks based on successful projects
Provide mechanical engineering expertise to validate AI-generated results and ensure engineering rigor
Qualifications
Must-haves:
Background in mechanical design engineering, ideally in a medium to large sized organization.
Strong understanding of PLM systems and enterprise engineering data architecture
Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and cross-functional collaborations
Experience working directly with customers or internal stakeholders to solve technical problems
Comfort working in fast-changing, ambiguous environments
Strong written communication and documentation skills
Working knowledge of high level AI architecture, specifically LLMs.
Familiarity with APIs, data integrations, and enterprise architecture concepts
Nice-to-haves:
Experience with internal tool development, scripting, or automation
Exposure to AI/ML tools applied to engineering workflows
Prior work in design consulting or product development at scale
Extra Details
This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package that includes stock options
Unlimited paid vacation, extended health benefits, and RRSP/401k matching
Remote-friendly within Eastern or Central time zones in Canada or the US.
This role will have a travel component to visit customers onsite. Customer visits are typically 1-3 days total, one or two a month.

About Chalk

Chalk is building the data platform that powers the future of machine learning applications. We tear down complexity, latency, and scale barriers that have traditionally constrained ML capabilities. Our platform combines Rust-speed performance with elegant tools that developers love to use. Leading companies depend on Chalk for everything from stopping fraudulent credit card swipes, verifying identities, and maximizing clean energy capture. We've recently raised a $50 million Series A https://www.reuters.com/business/databricks-competitor-chalk-raises-50-million-series-2025-05-28/, led by Felicis.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Chalk is the AI data platform built for inference. Customers come to us for two halves of the same problem: the context their models and agents run on, and the runtime they run in. Both sit inside the customer's own cloud.

Forward Deployed Strategists owns the technical direction of Chalk’s integrations: what gets built, in what order, and whether it holds up. You sit alongside sales, delivery, account management, and support on your accounts, and you’re the technical judge across all of it.

You’ll work closely with FDEs, who build directly with customer engineering teams. Some of that work is model-driven: fraud, payments, underwriting, recommendations, pricing. Increasingly it is agentic. Investigation agents that sit alongside data scientists, workflow automation, trust and safety, customer support, all of it running against real production context inside the customer's own environment.

Most problems start with the customer's architecture rather than ours. You will be asked to weigh in on systems Chalk does not touch. The bar for this role is architectural depth and judgment.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Run technical discovery: get inside how a customer's systems work, what is breaking, and what they are trying to ship

 - Advise on their architecture and their plans, including the migration path off whatever they run today. Tell them plainly what will break, what to sequence first, and what is not worth doing

 - Design what they build on Chalk, and set the bar it has to clear on correctness, latency, and cost

 - Design agentic solutions on Chalk: what an agent is allowed to reach, how it gets evaluated against real production context before it ships, and how it runs safely inside the customer's own cloud

 - Design, scope, and execute tight POCs. Pick the one thing worth proving, define what a clean result looks like before anyone starts, and keep the scope from drifting

 - Answer the questions a customer's principal engineers ask in week three. Partner with sales on the accounts where the decision is being made

 - Find the work worth doing next, and judge honestly whether it is a fit

 - Break work into projects with clear owners and dates, and hand the deep build work to the delivery engineers who will do it

 - Work with account management and support to keep the technical direction of an account coherent once it is live

 - Take what you learn in the field back to product and engineering, and argue for the changes that matter


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Real depth in production infrastructure, and a feel for how systems carrying live traffic actually fail

 - You have advised engineering teams on systems you did not build, and they took the advice

 - Technical taste. You have opinions about how systems should be built and you can defend them against people who have opinions of their own

 - You know how to scope a POC that proves the thing and nothing else, and you have said no to the ones that were never going to prove anything

 - Strong Python and SQL. You build prototypes and reference implementations, and you can read a customer's codebase and hold a conversation about it

 - Willing to tell a customer the thing they do not want to hear, including that a plan of theirs is wrong

 - You work well across a team. This role only functions if sales, delivery, account management, and support all trust your read

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, problem-solving, storytelling, and analytical skills


BONUS POINTS

All optional. None of these are required.

 - Experience deploying software into a customer's own cloud

 - Experience getting AI agents to run reliably against real production systems and real data

 - Domain depth in fraud, payments, underwriting, identity, recommendations, pricing, or logistics

 - Rust or C++
